usageNotes: Permanently removes a cluster-wide firewall rule at the specified zero-based position; the operation takes effect immediately and requires `Sys.Modify` on `/`. Always fetch the current rule list first to confirm the target position, since rules shift after any deletion. Pass the `digest` from the current ruleset to guard against concurrent modifications overwriting each other.

examples.summary: Delete the third cluster firewall rule (position 2), with digest guard

destructiveReason: Permanently deletes the cluster firewall rule at the given position; no undo is available and all cluster nodes immediately lose the traffic control that rule provided.
tips: Rule positions are zero-indexed and compact — deleting position 2 shifts all higher-index rules down by one.
Retrieve the current ruleset with get_cluster_firewall_rules first; its response includes the digest you should pass here.
Omitting `pos` targets position 0 (the first rule) — always supply an explicit position to avoid accidental deletions.
This endpoint returns null on success; treat a 200 with no body as confirmation.
